about: How Vesqira recognises a run of a tool and which of its outputs fill which generic role (ADR 0068, item 1). A profile only declares: a file and a key inside it that identify a run, and the names the tool gives its outputs. Reading the file, validating values and registering outputs stay in Vesqira's own code, and a profile never runs anything. What it supplies is labelled profile:<name>@<version>, never verified. Generic roles are the ids in 'roles'; an output a tool names that fits none of them is a declared extra, shown by the tool's own name. The orientation conventions (header cards) of the same tool are in the worker's orientation_profiles.json, linked by the 'orientation' name (one file for both is the consolidation step recorded in ADR 0068).
